App storage: a Storage holds its folder and opens the folders inside it, so no consumer takes a store and a path. Storage and IStorageProvider, in VpnHood.Net.Toolkit.Storages, take IAppFileStore's place: the provider keeps small text files by full path (FileSystemStorageProvider, moved from AppLib; on tvOS, KeyValueFileStore's entries of the defaults), and a Storage joins a name to its folder, refusing a path, ".." or a name with ':' (rooted on Windows), so whoever holds one stays inside its folder. AppOptionsContext makes Storage and NoBackupStorage over its one StorageProvider, so on tvOS both share its budget. AppSettingsService, the split lists, VpnProfileService, AppPersistState, ProxyEndPointCopy, the install id and PortalAuthenticationProvider each take a Storage and name their own files; the full paths are the same, so the files and tvOS's keys stay where they were. Breaking: AppOptionsContext.FileStore is StorageProvider, with Storage and NoBackupStorage beside it; PortalAuthenticationProvider takes a Storage in place of the store and the folder (each CONNECT head passes context.NoBackupStorage), as AppSettingsService and VpnProfileService do; IAppFileStore, FileSystemFileStore and TryReadJson are IStorageProvider, FileSystemStorageProvider and StorageExtensions.TryReadJson in VpnHood.Net.Toolkit.Storages. Docs: architecture-and-ipc.md. Checked: the app library's suite, the split tests and a new StorageTest (a name, never a path; nested storages write where the full paths did); CONNECT's six heads and the iOS library build.
